selected.title: The emergence of persister cells is repressed by TNFα treatment
paragraphs: Because the BCL11B+ cancer cells express various disparate drug-resistant programs that would require multiple therapeutics for targeting, we therefore asked whether there was a way to directly inhibit the BCL11B+ cell state and whether this could be a therapeutic approach against chemoresistance. To search for functional regulators of the Bcl11b+ cells, we analyzed the bulk RNA-seq data of Bcl11b+ and Bcl11b− cells and identified tumor necrosis factor–α (TNFα) signaling as the top-enriched pathway in Bcl11b− cells (Fig. 5A). This finding was corroborated by the analyses of scRNA-seq data of tumor organoids and bulk RNA-seq data of WT and Bcl11b KO tumor cells (Fig. 5B). TNFα, a pro-inflammatory factor, plays a physiological role in regulating mammary gland development (69) and can signal through diverse pathways including nuclear factor NF-κB (nuclear factor κB) and MEK/ERK [MAPK (mitogen-activated protein kinase) kinase/extracellular signal–regulated kinase] pathways (70). Notably, single-cell analyses of normal mammary epithelium and the tumor organoid revealed an inverse expression pattern of Bcl11b and Tnf, which itself is induced downstream of TNFα signaling (fig. S11A) (71). Tnfaip2, a primary response gene of TNFα signaling (72), is also specifically enriched in Bcl11b-negative cells (fig. S11A). In human breast cancer, we also observed that TNF expression is predominantly confined to BCL11B− cancer cells and several niche cell populations (fig. S11B). Thus, we hypothesize that TNFα, which is mainly secreted by luminal cells and niche cells (fig. S11B) (26, 73), could function as a natural inhibitor of the Bcl11b+ cell state.

To test this, we first used a murine mammary epithelial cell line Comma-Dβ, which exhibits heterogeneous expression of BCL11B. Flow cytometric analysis revealed that TNFα treatment induced a dose-dependent decrease in the proportion of BCL11B+ cells (fig. S11C). This repression is primarily mediated through the MEK/ERK pathway, as targeted inhibition of this cascade specifically rescued BCL11B expression from TNFα-mediated down-regulation (fig. S11, D and E). Induced overexpression of BCL11B, in turn, markedly attenuated TNFα-induced ERK activation in these cells (fig. S11, F and G). This observation is consistent with the recent characterization of BCL11B as a broad antagonist that suppresses TNFα and NF-κB signaling through upstream pathway inhibition (74). Together, these results reveal a previously unrecognized reciprocal inhibitory loop between TNFα signaling and BCL11B in mammary epithelial cells, a mechanism that likely contributes to the homeostatic counterbalance between the BCL11B+ state and TNFα signaling activity. Notably, while the Comma-Dβ cell line does not fully recapitulate the tumor context and TNFα-mediated repression of BCL11B is partial in these cells, this system nevertheless provides a useful platform for the mechanistic dissection of this regulatory axis.

We then exposed PyMT tumor organoids to TNFα treatment and observed a significant reduction in the number of BCL11B+ tumor cells within a few days (Fig. 5, C and D). The percentage of KRT14+ cells correspondingly decreased in the posttreatment tumor organoids (Fig. 5, C and D). Inhibition of the MEK/ERK pathway also effectively blocked the TNFα-induced downregulation of Bcl11b mRNA expression in the organoids (fig. S11H). We next treated single Bcl11btdTomato-positive tumor cells with TNFα and tracked the fates of these single cells. In the absence of TNFα, single BCL11B+ cells developed into tumor organoids with a prominent population of KRT14+ basal-like cells among the luminal cells (fig. S12A). Treatment with TNFα did not compromise the organoid formation efficiency but notably decreased the proportion of KRT14+/BCL11B+ basal-like cells within the formed organoids (fig. S12, B and C). This indicates a TNFα-induced basal-to-luminal lineage shift in the tumor cells. Pretreatment with TNFα effectively decreased the emergence of drug-resistant persister cells (Fig. 5, E and F), supporting the idea that impairing the BCL11B+ cell state can avert the development of drug resistance in breast cancer.

To assess the therapeutic potential of the TNFα combination treatment in vivo, we administered three doses of TNFα in conjunction with three cycles of Doxo to tumor-bearing recipient mice (Fig. 5G). TNFα injection was given at a tolerated dose on the basis of mouse studies and human clinical trials (75, 76) and was started before the chemotherapy treatment to eradicate BCL11B+ tumor cells before chemotherapy was administered. TNFα administration alone did not induce noticeable alterations in tumor growth or the overall health of the mice. However, when combined with Doxo, TNFα substantially enhanced the efficacy of chemotherapy in suppressing the growth of the WT tumors (Fig. 5G). The combination of TNFα and Doxo had no synergistic effects on Bcl11b-deficient tumor cells, suggesting that TNFα mainly functioned through targeting of the BCL11B+ cells (Fig. 5G). Analysis of the on-treatment and posttreatment samples revealed that Doxo exposure caused a significant decrease in cell proliferation in the tumor, although residual zones of Ki67+ cells were consistently observed during the treatment (Fig. 5H and fig. S12D). BCL11B+ cells were also found to be enriched in these residual lesions (Fig. 5H and fig. S12E). In contrast, treatment with a combination of TNFα and Doxo eliminated both BCL11B+ cells and residual proliferating cells (Fig. 5H and fig. S12, D and E). Together, these results reveal that pretreatment with TNFα before chemotherapy can strongly enhance chemotherapy efficacy by impairing the BCL11B+ cell state and preventing the emergence of cancer persisters.

selected.title: Quantification and statistical analysis
paragraphs: Data values are represented as the means ± standard error (SEM). P values are calculated using a t test, Wilcoxon rank-sum test, or two-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) test. Survival was measured using the Kaplan-Meier method. Each experiment has been replicated at least three times. For animal studies, the sample size was not predetermined to ensure adequate power to detect a prespecified effect size. No animals were excluded from analyses, experiments were not randomized, and investigators were not blinded to allocation during experiments.
